interventions.body:
Hello, I am EXPERT-EAU. I will now search the guidelines regarding management after a prostate biopsy.

**GUIDELINE**
"lm.nih.gov/pubmed/24762693 462. Pilatz, A., et al. Antibiotic Prophylaxis for the Prevention of Infectious Complications following Prostate Biopsy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Urol, 2020. 204: 224. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/32105195 463. European Medicines Agency. Disabling and potentially permanent side effects lead to suspension or restrictions of quinolone and fluoroquinolone antibiotics. 2019. 2021 p. EMA/175398/2019. https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/referrals/quinolone-fluoroquinolone-containing-medicinal-products 464. Carignan, A., et al. Effectiveness of fosfomycin tromethamine prophylaxis in preventing infection following transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate needle biopsy: Results from a large Canadian cohort. J Glob Antimicrob Resist, 2019. 17: 112. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/30553114 465. Wegelin, O., et al. Effectiveness of fosfomycin tromethamine prophylaxis in preventing infection following transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate needle biopsy: Results from a large Canadian cohort. J Glob Antimicrob Resist, 2019. 17: 112."

**WHAT THE EXPERTS DO NOT SETTLE**
The experts have not settled on a definitive action regarding active treatment, as the benefit node for treatment had an AUC of 0.5645, which is at chance level, indicating no informed discrimination.

**WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE**
The documents must settle on the appropriate management strategy following the biopsy, specifically concerning the role of MRI, repeat biopsy, and the decision pathway based on the findings.

{"case_id": "T2-002", "radiology_report": "Spaarne Gasthuis (Haarlem)
Radiology Dept
Date: 20 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (187.0 ng/mL), prior biopsy Gleason 4+4, evaluate for local extent and suspicious lesions.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 57.28 mL.
T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone, extending towards the right seminal vesicle. On diffusion-weighted imaging, the lesion shows marked restricted diffusion with high signal intensity on b=1400 images and corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense enhancement of the lesion relative to the surrounding glandular tissue. The right seminal vesicle shows asymmetrical enlargement and signal alteration consistent with tumour infiltration. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or bone lesions are identified within the field of view.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone with seminal vesicle involvement.
Prostate volume 57.28 mL; PSA density 3.26 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.964853."}
